items.title: Lew Tabackin interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: I mean look at some of Dizzy Gillespie’s stuff. Some people transcribe it. It’s impossible. Dizzy wouldn’t even know where to start and nobody else would.

ctx.x: It’s not supposed to be read.

I mean if you look at the stuff people have played, I mean look at some of Dizzy Gillespie’s stuff. Some people transcribe it. It’s impossible. Dizzy wouldn’t even know where to start and nobody else would. I mean that’s why improvised music is so wonderful. Sometimes you kind of like transcend your abilities. Like sometimes when things are really happening, you say where did this come from? I mean I never practiced this, I never thought about it, it just comes. And like you do things that you can never recreate,…
Well that’s a good note to end on. And I appreciate your time today. It’s been fascinating talking to you and you’ve expressed some things in a way I haven’t heard before.
